sources.title: Amur and Okhotsk Tungus in The Peoples of Northeast Asia through Time
sources.note: Scholarly historical chapter distinguishing Negidal, eastern Evenki, and Okhotsk Even trajectories rather than one timeless people.

sources.title: Language contact in northeastern Siberia
sources.note: Peer-reviewed overview of documented seventeenth-century distributions and cautious hypotheses about earlier Tungusic and Sakha movements.

sources.title: On the Position of the Small Houses Culture in the Periodization of Medieval Yakutia
sources.note: Irkutsk State University review of a disputed thirteenth-century attribution, four known settlements, later evidence, buildings, pottery, and animal bones.

sources.title: The Mongol campaign against forest peoples in 1207
sources.note: Russian Academy study locating the campaign principally toward Oirat and Yenisei Kyrgyz regions and discussing source disagreement.

sources.title: A little-known Mongol military expedition to the Yenisei in 1207
sources.note: National University of Mongolia article analyzing the campaign, its goals, and its western forest-people geography.

sources.title: A Note on the Forest People: Siberia under the Mongol Empire
sources.note: Academic article on the varied northern peoples grouped by Mongol sources as forest people.

sources.title: A study of dwelling forms among Tungusic-speaking communities
sources.note: Architectural study comparing later documented dwelling forms among Manchurian, Xibo, Nanai, Orochon, and Evenki communities.

sources.title: Evenki ecological houses and community settlements
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of later Evenki structures made with locally available wood, bark, and hides for severe seasonal weather.

sources.title: Ethnoarchaeology of Evenki reindeer herding and hunting
sources.note: Peer-reviewed ethnoarchaeological study warning that recent Evenki practices cannot simply date or explain early reindeer pastoralism.

sources.title: Origins of reindeer riding in Inner Asia
sources.note: Collaborative archaeology study emphasizing regional variation and uncertainty in the timing and growth of reindeer riding.

sources.title: The system of Evenki ecological knowledge
sources.note: Community-collaborative ethnography of later Evenki seasonal work, fishing, herd care, sharing, insects, landscape, and teaching.

sources.title: Plant Hunting: Evenki Medicines in Northern Baikal
sources.note: Russian Academy ethnography of modern Northern Baikal medicinal-plant knowledge, mobility, observation, scarcity, prevention, and treatment.

sources.title: Food Plants in Evenki Culture
sources.note: Siberian Federal University synthesis of modern ethnobotanical knowledge, gathering, food, ritual, medicine, and cultural identity.

sources.title: Gender Distinctions in an Egalitarian Society: The Case of Evenki People
sources.note: Fieldwork-based study of situational gender roles and personal autonomy in a modern Baikal Evenki community.

sources.title: Companionship among the Evenki of Eastern Buryatia
sources.note: Max Planck working paper describing companionship and flexible social organization from modern fieldwork.

sources.title: A Medieval Yakut Burial near Lake Atlasovskoye
sources.note: Russian Academy study of a fourteenth- or fifteenth-century burial and paleopathology, later than and west of the exact target evidence.

sources.title: The Earliest Jurchen Inscription from Arkhara
sources.note: Russian Academy report on a securely dated 1127 Jurchen inscription from a locality south of the target and before its interval.

sources.title: Phonology of the Jurchen language
sources.note: Linguistic study identifying Jurchen as the earliest Tungusic language with native-script materials while stressing limited evidence.

sources.title: Tangaralaakh sanctuary and rock imagery in northern Yakutia
sources.note: Archaeological review separating images from several periods, uncertain medieval marks, later repainting, offerings, and modern hunter traditions.

sources.title: Open Indigenous knowledge resources for climate adaptation
sources.note: UNESCO education project recognizing living Indigenous language and environmental knowledge as integrated, community-held systems.

sources.title: The Peoples of Northeast Asia through Time
sources.note: Brill scholarly book framing Northeast Asian histories through changing coastal, river, language, and community relationships.

sources.title: Languages of Northern Eurasia
sources.note: Cambridge overview distinguishing Tungusic, Mongolic, Turkic, and unrelated northern Eurasian language families and distributions.

sources.title: Archaeological heritage of the Sakha Republic
sources.note: Russian Academy catalog synthesizing protected and identified archaeological sites across Yakutia through the late medieval period.
